title: Swap through pointers
description:
Write `swapValues(a, b)`. It is given the addresses of two `int` variables and exchanges their values.

After `swapValues(&x, &y)`, `x` holds what `y` held and `y` holds what `x` held.

The function receives addresses, so it has to work on the values **at** those addresses. `std::swap` is not allowed here: write the three steps yourself.
hints: If you write `*a = *b;` first, the original value of `*a` is gone. Copy it into an ordinary `int` variable before that line.
The three steps are: keep `*a`, copy `*b` into `*a`, copy the kept value into `*b`.
Assigning to `a` or `b` without the `*` only changes the function's own copies of the addresses. It does nothing to the caller's variables.
rules: Write the swap yourself, using the pointers.
